name: Lemaître’s expansion and nebular velocities
description: Lemaître related a nonstatic relativistic cosmological model to available nebular distances and radial velocities.

events.statement: An English translation of the 1927 paper appeared in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society in 1931 after Eddington supported publication.

evidence.supports: Uses Lemaître’s correspondence to describe Eddington’s encouragement, the 1931 English translation and the author’s omission of the earlier numerical discussion.

contributions.resource: Translated the paper and omitted the older provisional velocity discussion.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode supported by the evidence collected here; not a global-priority claim.

caveats: Historical estimates depend on grouping and distance calibration; Slipher supplied many velocities via Strömberg. Hubble’s 1929 analysis is distinct. Whether Lemaître knew Friedmann’s 1922 work is not established here. Lemaître’s own correspondence, as reported in the cited history, identifies him as translator and explains the omission of the older numerical discussion; access to the English version alone cannot establish the original 1927 coefficient.
